A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we introduced a useful heuristic for equitability, showed that it is satisfied by MIC and not mutual information estimates, and provided a large-scale evaluation of these statistics under a wide variety of noise models and sample sizes.
MIC is more equitable in practice than mutual information estimates under a broad set of noise models, and that the gap in equitability widens as sample size decreases.

we have established that MIC is more equitable in many settings than mutual information estimation, and that it is the only known statistic that is both more equitable than mutual-information estimation and is also computationally tractable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the equitability of a statistic matters, and that MIC is more equitable for many data exploration tasks than mutual information estimation.
MIC is a promising new statistic with a strong theoretical basis, and it has already been used in many applications.
